summary: Server-only results of the 'mon' (EocServerMonitor, a debug monitor) request mon::InvalidTeleporterRequestComponent. Registered in App::InitServer (bg3.exe+0x11F0480, size 0x10, align 0x10) with the SAME destructor as mon::InvalidInteractableResultsComponent (bg3.exe+0x11F15C0 -> 0x11F15D0), so the two share one layout: an Array of 48-byte elements starting with a string. No system of bg3.exe or of the Toolkit DLLs reads or writes it (the monitor implementation is not shipped). Never seen alive.

fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: destructor bg3.exe+0x11F15D0 (jumped to from bg3.exe+0x11F15C0, registered by bg3.exe+0x11F0480) walks the elements with stride 0x30 and frees a 24-byte game string at +0 of each (capacity u32 at +0x14 > 0xF -> free; resets size +0x10 = 0, capacity = 0xF).

fields.name: field_18
fields.evidence: trivially destructible remainder of the 0x30-byte element; nothing in bg3.exe writes or reads it. macOS destructor (bg3_macos_x64+0x25DAB90) uses stride 0x28 (string + 16 bytes): the Windows tail is 8 bytes longer - unknown content.

fields.name: Results
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x11F15D0: Array{ptr +0, capacity u32 +8, size u32 +0xC}; element stride 0x30 and its string member from the destructor loop; registry size 16 (server row).

open_questions: The 24 bytes after the string in each element (no producer exists in bg3.exe or the Toolkit DLLs).
Whether the macOS stride 0x28 vs Windows 0x30 hides a 16-aligned member in the tail.
status_reason: no live or captured instance: needs a situation that creates it
second_pass: Cannot be settled from code: the second pass found no producer or consumer anywhere - bg3.exe has only the type registration (App::CreateECS -> bg3.exe+0x11EExxx), the static type-name initialiser and the component ops; the macOS build has only ComponentOps/ComponentSignals/destructor instantiations (macos_index.py names '<mon::' lists just the eight mon types) and the Toolkit DLLs mention them only in App::AddGlobalSwitchesToOptionDialog. The shapes from the creator/destructor stand; the members stay unknown.
